findings.text: the parenthetical that "only tests/ differs between base and head (git diff 77c20349..HEAD -- . ':(exclude)tests/' is empty)" is false at the head this review names: that command returns three paths at ed2054cc (docs/plans/the-suite-is-green-at-head.html, docs/evidence/archive/the-suite-is-green-at-head-landed.html and docs/figures/the-suite-is-green-at-head/repair-classes-by-node-id.svg) because the node lands its plan, archive and figure records inside the same range; the product-side claim the sentence needs is git diff 77c20349..ed2054cc -- reckon/, which is empty and which is what this review checked, so the substance holds while the named instrument does not, and the same quoted command stands in the control log's header, so a reader re-running the record's own check gets a non-empty result.

(repeated at line 17 and, at the reviewed head, in docs/plans/the-suite-is-green-at-head.html:80 and docs/evidence/archive/the-suite-is-green-at-head-landed.html:106) the claim that every log header names the resolved reckon.__file__ that was imported is not true of the seven base-*.log files this manifest lists in test_logs: those seven carry no header at all, so nothing in the cited receipt shows which product tree they imported; the pin claim is true of the seven head logs and of the control log's header, and the base pass was in fact pinned (its invocation points PYTHONPATH at the worker's own worktree, and the control reproduces its ids exactly), so the substance holds and the sentence overstates what the cited receipts contain.

the record's plan-commits meta lists five commits, omitting e1785677, which created this node's section, and ed2054cc (this head), which last edited the file, so the record's own provenance is not recoverable from the record; the run's manifest carries all seven commits.

item_verdicts.diff: read all seven commits against 77c20349; the change is seven test files plus the plan, archive and figure records, no test function is removed except the records' own documented rename, no skip or xfail is added, and the repaired ids were re-expressed against the shipped behaviour rather than loosened.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when requires each owned file run in its own process with its own --basetemp, its pre-repair version observed red at 77c20349, and the red set to be exactly the ids section 4 lists for the node; the seven base logs hold those seventeen ids, the negative control reproduces them from a base tree I verified file-identical to git show 77c20349, and base and head collect the same number of ids per file, so nothing was skipped, xfailed or deleted; one addition from my own re-runs is recorded under evidence and in the findings below.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that the test files the research record's section 4 lists for this node pass at the node's head; at ed2054cc sixteen of the seventeen owned ids are green and the seventeenth is carried in follow_ons as a product defect with file, lines, behaviour and a reproduction, which the done_when permits; I re-ran all seven owned files from this node's own tree at ed2054cc and reproduced every head result it records (6, 14, 4, 12, 1, 6 passed, and 1 failed / 5 passed).
item_verdicts.manifest: read in full; it states a class and cause for each owned id, the renamed id with its reason, and the remaining product defect with file, line and a reproduction, all of which I re-read at the head or reproduced; two statements the record makes about its own log evidence do not hold as written (findings below).
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared scope is the ten paths in the run's orientation_write_paths; the eight paths in git diff --name-only 77c20349..ed2054cc are all inside it, git diff 77c20349..ed2054cc -- reckon/ is empty, and the worktree is clean at ed2054cc with no stash.

justifications.durability: the repairs assert shipped behaviour instead of literals (the claim-walk count is read from the owner's own record, the stub launcher's pid is live, the runtime root is built under the case's own temp dir); the record reports test_crew_dispatch_arming as plainly passing while one of its ids failed once in three isolated re-runs of mine under load.
justifications.evidence: both sides were measured per file with per-file basetemps under a control whose first line is the declared string, whose ids match the base logs exactly, and whose base tree I verified file-identical to git show 77c20349, and the node caught its own first-pass drift and re-ran both sides pinned; deducted for two provenance statements about its own logs that do not hold as written.
justifications.fit: the repairs follow the file-local fixture idiom of the files they touch, the class-and-cause vocabulary matches the plan's class list, the figure partitions all seventeen ids by class, and the run rules (one process per file, its own basetemp, on compute) were followed.
justifications.goal_fidelity: sixteen of the seventeen owned ids pass at ed2054cc under my own re-run and the seventeenth is carried outward with its file, line and reproduction, which the done_when allows.
justifications.scope_discipline: all eight changed paths lie inside the ten declared write paths, nothing under reckon/ differs between base and head, and the tree is clean at the head with no stash.
